--- title: "Metric Analysis" format: html: fig-dpi: 200 code-fold: true editor_options: chunk_output_type: console warnings: false execute: cache: false --- ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} options(scipen = 999) pacman::p_load( conflicted, dplyr, htmltools, stringr, tidyr, reactable, purrr, broom, knitr, kableExtra, tictoc, furrr, parallelly, splm, spdep, spatialreg, sf, skimr, ggplot2, ggpubr, readr, lmtest, sandwich, performance, snakecase, ggtext ) pacman::p_load_gh( 'Food-Systems-Research-Institute/SMdata', 'Food-Systems-Research-Institute/SMdocs' ) conflicts_prefer( dplyr::select(), dplyr::filter(), dplyr::pull(), stats::lag(), base::setdiff(), .quiet = TRUE ) dp_meta <- readRDS(here::here("0_prep", "output", "dp_meta.rds")) dp_weights <- readRDS(here::here("0_prep", "output", "dp_weights.rds")) dp_metrics_county_adj <- readRDS(here::here("0_prep", "output", "dp_metrics_county_adj.rds")) dp_metrics_state_adj <- readRDS(here::here("0_prep", "output", "dp_metrics_state_adj.rds")) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: This page explores time series data at the state and county level, then runs some regressions to see whether metrics are improving or declining over time at the county level. We first run weighted OLS models with robust SEs. Then we use spatial error models weighted by both geography and weighting variables. ## Time Series Plot time series of each metric that has at least two data points. These are unweighted values. LOESS curves are shown in blue, while individual county/state data are shown in black ### County Data First, we prepare a vector names of our time series variables for counties: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Prepare vector of county variables that are time series str(dp_metrics_county_adj) vars <- unique(dp_metrics_county_adj$variable_name) series_vars <- map(vars, ~ { count <- dp_metrics_county_adj %>% filter(variable_name == .x) %>% pull(year) %>% unique() %>% length() if (count > 1) { return(.x) } else { return(NULL) } }) %>% keep(~ !is.null(.x)) %>% unlist() dir.create('5_trends/output/trend_plots', recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE) saveRDS(series_vars, '5_trends/output/series_vars.rds') ``` ::: Now we plot each graph individually and arrange them together: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plots <- map(series_vars, ~ { df <- dp_metrics_county_adj %>% filter(variable_name == .x) %>% ggplot(aes(x = year, y = value)) + geom_line( aes(group = fips), alpha = 0.3 ) + geom_smooth( method = 'loess', lwd = 2 ) + labs( x = 'Year', title = .x ) + theme_classic() }) ggarrange( plotlist = plots, ncol = 4, nrow = 11 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](dp_trends_files/figure-html/county_time_series-1.png){width=2400} ::: ::: ### State Data Again, start by getting a vector of time series metrics for state data, then plot all metrics: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} vars <- unique(dp_metrics_state_adj$variable_name) state_series_vars <- map(vars, ~ { count <- dp_metrics_state_adj %>% filter(variable_name == .x) %>% pull(year) %>% unique() %>% length() if (count > 1) { return(.x) } else { return(NULL) } }) %>% keep(~ !is.null(.x)) %>% unlist() saveRDS(state_series_vars, '5_trends/output/state_series_vars.rds') plots <- map(state_series_vars, ~ { df <- dp_metrics_state_adj %>% filter(variable_name == .x) %>% mutate(across(c(year, value), as.numeric)) %>% ggplot(aes(x = year, y = value)) + geom_line( aes(group = fips), alpha = 0.3 ) + geom_smooth( method = 'loess', lwd = 2 ) + labs( x = 'Year', title = .x ) + theme_classic() }) ggarrange( plotlist = plots, ncol = 3, nrow = 5 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` $`1` ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](dp_trends_files/figure-html/state_time_series-1.png){width=2400} ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` $`2` ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](dp_trends_files/figure-html/state_time_series-2.png){width=2400} ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` attr(,"class") [1] "list" "ggarrange" ``` ::: ::: ### Tiny Trend Graphs Outputs not shown here - these will be added to a table in the paper. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} all_series_vars <- c(series_vars, state_series_vars) # Function to get tiny plots from county and state vars get_tiny_plots <- function(df, vars) { map(vars, ~ { df <- df %>% filter(variable_name == .x, !is.na(value)) %>% ggplot(aes(x = year, y = value)) + geom_line( aes(group = fips), alpha = 0.25, color = 'grey', linewidth = 0.5 ) + geom_smooth( method = "loess", se = FALSE, linewdith = 0.75 ) + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(2000, 2024)) + scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) + scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) + theme_bw() + theme( axis.text = element_blank(), axis.title = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major = element_blank(), plot.margin = margin(rep(0.5, 4)) ) }) %>% setNames(c(vars)) } # Plots for counties county_plots <- dp_metrics_county_adj %>% get_tiny_plots( vars = series_vars ) # Plots for states state_plots <- dp_metrics_state_adj %>% get_tiny_plots( vars = state_series_vars ) # One more plot for CPI - food at home system_plots <- SMdata::metrics %>% filter(variable_name == 'cpiFoodAtHome') %>% get_tiny_plots(vars = 'cpiFoodAtHome') # Save them all to outputs with variable names iwalk(c(county_plots, state_plots, system_plots), \(plot, var) { ggsave( filename = paste0('5_trends/output/trend_plots/fig_trend_', var, '.png'), plot = plot, width = 1.5, height = 1.5, units = 'cm', dpi = 300, bg = NULL ) }) ``` ::: ## Spatial Regressions {#sec-ols} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} str(dp_metrics_county_adj) vars <- unique(dp_metrics_county_adj$variable_name) dp_metrics_county_adj_normed <- map(vars, ~ { dp_metrics_county_adj %>% filter(variable_name == .x) %>% mutate(across(c(year, value), as.numeric)) %>% drop_na(value) %>% group_by(variable_name) %>% mutate(normed_value = min_max(value)) %>% ungroup() }) %>% list_rbind() str(dp_metrics_county_adj_normed) dir.create('5_trends/output/', recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE) saveRDS(dp_metrics_county_adj_normed, '5_trends/output/dp_metrics_county_adj_normed.rds') ``` ::: Create a weights crosswalk that links `variable_name`s to weighting variables. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} weights_crosswalk <- data.frame( metric = c( 'GDP', 'GDP from agriculture', 'Total number of producers', 'Total number of operations', 'Population (annual)', 'Population (5 year)', 'Population (5 year, smooth)', 'Acres of land', 'Acres of water', 'Area under agriculture (CDL)', 'Number employed in agriculture', 'Acres operated', 'Acres operated, smooth', 'Acres of cropland ag land', 'Acres of woodland ag land', 'Acres of pasture ag land', 'Total farm income', 'Total sales from commodities' ), variable_name = c( 'gdp', 'gdpFromAg', 'nProducers', 'nOperations', 'populationAnnual', 'population5Year', 'population5YearSmooth', 'landAcres', 'waterAcres', 'cdlAgAcres', 'annualAvgEmplvlNAICS11', 'acresOperated', 'acresOperatedSmooth', 'agLandCropAcres', 'agLandWoodAcres', 'agLandPastureAcres', 'totalFarmIncome', 'totalSalesCommodities' ) ) # Link weight vars to the appropriate variables weights_crosswalk <- dp_meta %>% select(variable_name, weighting) %>% filter(variable_name %in% dp_metrics_county_adj_normed$variable_name) %>% left_join(weights_crosswalk, by = join_by(weighting == metric)) %>% setNames(c('variable_name', 'weight_metric', 'weight_variable')) %>% select(-weight_metric) %>% na.omit() head(weights_crosswalk) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 2 variable_name weight_variable 1 landValPerAcre totalFarmIncome 2 annualAvgWklyWageNAICS11 gdp 3 gini population5YearSmooth 4 totalIndemnities totalFarmIncome 5 expPF gdpFromAg 6 totalEcosystemCarbonPerAcre landAcres ``` ::: ::: ### Models Spatial error models with the `spatialreg` package. We are now working with: $$ \Large y = X\beta + u, u = \lambda Wu + \epsilon, $$ where $y$ are normalized metric values, $X$ is an $n * k$ matrix, $\beta$ is a vector of predictors, $u$ is the spatial autocorrelation error term, $\lambda$ is the spatial error parameter, $W$ is the county weights matrix, and $\epsilon$ is the error term. We run this portion of the code in parallel because it has a pretty long run time. Again, results are saved so it doesn't need to be run again unless something changes. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Slow. Run only when the saved models are missing # or older than the step-0 input, else load. Delete .rds to force rerun sar_path <- '5_trends/output/errorsarlm_outs.rds' in_path <- here::here('0_prep', 'output', 'dp_metrics_county_adj.rds') stale <- !file.exists(sar_path) || file.mtime(sar_path) < file.mtime(in_path) if (stale) { dir.create('5_trends/output', recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE) state_link <- SMdata::fips_key %>% filter(str_length(fips) == 2, fips != '00') %>% select(fips, state_code) dat <- dp_metrics_county_adj %>% pivot_wider( id_cols = fips:year, names_from = variable_name, values_from = value, # TODO: better way to collapse values_fn = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE) ) %>% filter(str_detect(fips, '^09', negate = TRUE)) %>% mutate(link = str_sub(fips, end = 2)) %>% left_join(state_link, by = join_by(link == fips)) %>% select(-link) %>% mutate(across(!c(fips, state_code), as.numeric)) vars <- names(dat)[!names(dat) %in% c('fips', 'year', 'state_code')] # County contiguity from county geometry county_sf <- SMdata::neast_counties_2024 %>% select(fips) %>% filter(str_detect(fips, '^09', negate = TRUE)) W_county <- nb2mat(poly2nb(county_sf), style = 'B', zero.policy = TRUE) dimnames(W_county) <- list(county_sf$fips, county_sf$fips) tic() # multicore (fork) if possible, otherwise multisession if (parallelly::supportsMulticore()) { plan(multicore, workers = 6) } else { plan(multisession, workers = 6) } sar_outs <- future_map(vars, \(var) { cat('\n\nStarting', var) tryCatch({ # Reduce to relevant variable, remove NAs df <- dat %>% select(fips, year, !!sym(var), state_code) %>% drop_na(!!sym(var)) %>% mutate(normed = min_max(!!sym(var))) # Regular weights. Unweighted vars are absent from the crosswalk weight_var <- weights_crosswalk$weight_variable[weights_crosswalk$variable_name == var] has_weight <- length(weight_var) == 1 && !is.na(weight_var) if (has_weight) { weight_df <- dp_weights %>% mutate( value = as.numeric(value), year = as.numeric(year) ) %>% rename( weight_value = value, weight_name = variable_name, weight_year = year ) %>% filter(weight_name == weight_var, str_length(fips) == 5) # Join weights back to df if (all(is.na(weight_df$weight_year))) { df <- df %>% inner_join(weight_df, by = join_by(fips)) } else { df <- df %>% inner_join(weight_df, by = join_by(fips, year == weight_year)) } cat('\nJoined to weights:', weight_var) } else { cat('\nNo weighting variable') } model_df <- df # Drop rows with missing weight. Record drop n_weight_dropped <- 0L if (has_weight) { na_wt <- is.na(model_df[['weight_value']]) n_weight_dropped <- sum(na_wt) if (n_weight_dropped > 0) { cat('\nDropping', n_weight_dropped, 'row(s) with NA weight_value') model_df <- model_df[!na_wt, , drop = FALSE] } } # Check if there are too few values or years n_years <- dplyr::n_distinct(model_df$year) n_vals <- dplyr::n_distinct(model_df[[var]]) if (n_years < 2 || n_vals < 2) { msg <- paste0( 'Issue with ', var, ': ', n_years, ' distinct year(s), ', n_vals, ' distinct value(s) reaching the model' ) warning(msg) return(msg) } # Report if state_code is NA. It shouldn't be if (anyNA(model_df$state_code)) { bad <- unique(model_df$fips[is.na(model_df$state_code)]) msg <- paste0( 'NA state_code ', var, ': ', length(bad), ' fips unmatched (', paste(head(bad), collapse = ', '), ')' ) warning(msg) return(msg) } fp <- model_df$fips # Stop if fips code not in fp stopifnot(all(fp %in% rownames(W_county))) W_stack <- W_county[fp, fp] # No cross-year links W_stack[outer(model_df$year, model_df$year, `!=`)] <- 0 diag(W_stack) <- 0 lw <- mat2listw(W_stack, style = 'W', zero.policy = TRUE) cat('\nCreated lw') # Assign weights arg if variable is weighted. Otherwise NULL if (has_weight) { weights_arg <- model_df[['weight_value']] } else { weights_arg <- NULL } # Run error sar model with appropriate (or no) weighting model <- errorsarlm( normed ~ as.numeric(year) + state_code, data = model_df, listw = lw, weights = weights_arg, zero.policy = TRUE ) cat('\nRan model') # Carry the NA-weight drop count with the model for reporting attr(model, 'n_weight_dropped') <- n_weight_dropped return(model) }, error = function(e) { return(paste0('Error with ', var, ': ', e)) } ) }, .progress = FALSE, .options = furrr_options(seed = TRUE)) %>% setNames(vars) plan(sequential) toc() saveRDS(sar_outs, sar_path) } # 5 minutes or so ``` ::: #### Reactable Table First we wrangle our outputs to get the relevant results in a nicely formatted table: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Reload so this chunk runs when interactive re-run sar_outs <- readRDS(sar_path) (start <- length(sar_outs)) sar_keeps <- sar_outs[names(sar_outs) != 'state_code'] %>% keep(~ inherits(.x, 'Sarlm')) (end <- length(sar_keeps)) (lost <- start - end) # 42 to 37 # Which are missing and why (lost_vars <- setdiff(names(sar_outs), names(sar_keeps))) (reasons <- sar_outs[lost_vars] %>% keep(is.character)) # Losing 5 that are actually single year # Weight rows dropped per model (weight_drops <- imap(sar_keeps, ~ { n <- attr(.x, 'n_weight_dropped') tibble(variable_name = .y, n_weight_rows_dropped = if (is.null(n)) 0L else n) }) %>% bind_rows() %>% filter(n_weight_rows_dropped > 0) %>% arrange(desc(n_weight_rows_dropped))) # These had issues with missing weights - just removed those rows sar_df <- imap(sar_keeps, ~ { tryCatch( { df <- tidy(.x) est <- df[2, 'estimate'] %>% as.numeric se <- df[2, 'std.error'] %>% as.numeric alpha <- 0.05 z <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2) confints <- c(est - z * se, est + z * se) # confints <- confint(.x)[3, ] out <- df %>% filter(str_detect(term, 'year')) %>% mutate( variable_name = .y, conf_low = confints[1], conf_high = confints[2] ) %>% select(-term) %>% mutate( sig = case_when( p.value < 0.001 ~ '***', p.value > 0.001 & p.value < 0.01 ~ '**', p.value > 0.01 & p.value < 0.05 ~ '*', p.value > 0.05 ~ ' ', .default = NA ) ) return(out) }, error = function(e) { message('Error') print(e) } ) }) %>% keep(is.data.frame) %>% bind_rows() str(sar_df) sar_df (lost_on_wrangle <- setdiff(names(sar_keeps), sar_df$variable_name)) (check <- sar_outs[names(sar_keeps) %in% lost_on_wrangle]) # No more lost sar_raw_outputs <- sar_df %>% mutate(trend = case_when( estimate > 0 & str_detect(sig, '\\*') ~ 'increasing', estimate < 0 & str_detect(sig, '\\*') ~ 'decreasing', str_detect(sig, '\\*', negate = TRUE) ~ 'no change', .default = NA_character_ )) str(sar_raw_outputs) # Bring in directional values. Keep only the ones without question marks, # clearly higher or lower str(dp_meta) directions <- dp_meta %>% filter(str_detect(desirable, 'higher|lower'), !is.na(variable_name)) %>% mutate(desirable = str_remove_all(desirable, '\\?')) %>% select(variable_name, desirable) reverse <- directions %>% filter(desirable == 'lower') %>% pull(variable_name) # Reduce to only vars that have a direction. # Here we lose a few metrics sar_model_outputs <- sar_raw_outputs %>% filter(variable_name %in% directions$variable_name) %>% mutate( reverse = ifelse(variable_name %in% reverse, TRUE, FALSE), outcome = case_when( reverse == FALSE & trend == 'increasing' ~ 'better', reverse == FALSE & trend == 'decreasing' ~ 'worse', reverse == TRUE & trend == 'increasing' ~ 'worse', reverse == TRUE & trend == 'decreasing' ~ 'better', trend == 'no change' ~ 'no change', .default = NA ), across(where(is.numeric), ~ format(round(.x, 3), nsmall = 3)) ) sar_model_outputs nrow(sar_model_outputs) # 33 (n_metrics <- dim(sar_model_outputs)[1]) # See what we lost (lost <- setdiff(sar_raw_outputs$variable_name, sar_model_outputs$variable_name)) (n_lost <- length(lost)) (print_lost <- lost %>% paste0(collapse = ', ')) # lost 4 without direction for better or worse # proportion getting better or worse (tab <- table(sar_model_outputs$outcome)) (percs <- round(prop.table(tab), 3) * 100) ``` ::: We have 33 metrics modeled. 45.5% are getting better, 18.2% are getting worse, and 18.2% are stable. We drop 4 metrics here that don't have proper directions (vacancyRate\, populationChangePerc\, annualPrecipCMSqKm\, ftmProdRatio). Now we present the table, including normative outcomes: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} sar_framed_outputs <- dp_meta %>% select(dimension, index, indicator, metric, variable_name) %>% right_join(sar_model_outputs, by = join_by(variable_name == variable_name)) ## Create interactive table for Quarto get_reactable( sar_framed_outputs, defaultPageSize = 10, columns = list( variable_name = colDef(minWidth = 200), sig = colDef(minWidth = 50), reverse = colDef(minWidth = 75), statistic = colDef(minWidth = 75), outcome = colDef(minWidth = 75) ) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: #### LaTeX Table Saving table to $\LaTeX$ for paper: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} str(sar_framed_outputs) # Reduce to specific columns latex_df <- sar_framed_outputs %>% select(metric, estimate:p.value, sig, outcome) %>% mutate( p.value = case_when( str_detect(sig, '\\*') ~ paste0(p.value, sig), .default = p.value ), outcome = case_when( outcome == 'no change' ~ '\\textemdash', .default = str_to_title(outcome) ) ) %>% select(-sig) %>% setNames(c( 'Metric', '$\\beta$', 'SE', '$z$-value', 'p-value', 'Outcome' )) str(latex_df) # Save to latex latex_df %>% kbl( format = 'latex', caption = 'Spatial error models of year and state on metric', label = 'tab_errorsarlm', booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE ) %>% kable_styling( font_size = 9 ) %>% footnote( general_title = "", general = '\\\\textit{Note: }The table shows coefficients of the effect of year on normalized, inflation-adjusted metrics with state as a covariate. Metrics are weighted by variables shown in Table \\\\ref{tab:tab_metrics_body}. Significant p-values indicated change over time, and the direction of the outcome was determined based on desirable directions of change for each metric. ***: p < 0.001, **: p < 0.01, *: p < 0.05.', threeparttable = TRUE, escape = FALSE ) %>% save_kable( file = '5_trends/output/tab_errorsarlm.tex' ) ``` ::: #### Figure Finally, the figure below shows coefficient estimates and confidence intervals for the errorsar models. Green points represent metrics that are trending in a "good" direction, while purple represents trends in a "bad" direction. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Using functions at top of script to process outputs and make graph errorsar_figure_data <- prepare_figure_data(model_output_df = sar_framed_outputs) errorsar_figure <- pct_change_graph( figure_data = errorsar_figure_data$figure_data, dp_text_palette = dp_text_palette, label_dimension_lookup = errorsar_figure_data$label_dimension_lookup ) ggsave( '5_trends/output/fig_errorsarlm.png', plot = errorsar_figure, width = 8.5, height = 6, units = 'in', bg = 'white' ) errorsar_figure ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](dp_trends_files/figure-html/errorsar_figure-1.png){width=1400} ::: :::
